title: Local irradiation of patient-derived tumors in immunodeficient mice
protocol: Calculate the volume and cells needed for the number of available mice, taking the total number of mice × 50 μL + minimal 300 μL for loss in syringe needle and spill.
Calculate the amount of Matrigel needed (50% of total volume).
Thaw Matrigel on ice, allowing it to become liquid.
Harvest patient-derived cells.
Remove medium from cells.
Wash flask with 2 mL (T25) or 5 mL (T75) PBS.
Add 5 mM EDTA in PBS for 2 min at 37°C if needed and remove.
Add 1 mL (T25) or 3 mL (T75) 1× trypsin for 3–10 min at 37°C.
Resuspend cells carefully with a long reach filter tip.
Check under microscope to ensure single-cell suspension is obtained.
Inactivate trypsin by adding CSC medium without serum and spin down cells at 300 × g for 3 min if using CSC medium.
Remove all medium and resuspend in 1–3 mL CSC medium if necessary.
Count the number of cells per mL, e.g., in a hemocytometer.
Take 1 × 10^5 cells in a total of 50 μL solution for injection.
Calculate volume of cell suspension needed: Total volume / (cells per mL / 1 × 10^5).
Resuspend 50% of cell suspension with 50% Matrigel on ice in a 5 mL round-bottom polystyrene tube.
Transport cell-Matrigel suspension on ice to the animal facility.
Keep cells in Matrigel on ice to avoid solidification.
Resuspend or flick the cell suspension tube right before mixing with Matrigel.
Randomize mice between different treatment groups.
Distribute mice of one litter across different treatment groups and ensure a similar number of males and females per treatment group.
Anesthetize mice with 2% Isoflurane in 100% oxygen for 5 minutes.
Mark animals for identification using earmarks or color marking.
Carefully remove the hair on the right hind limb of all the mice by shaving.
Disinfect the skin with Virkon.
Resuspend pre-made cell suspension from previous steps.
Fill a 1 mL syringe immediately after resuspending the cell suspension and attach a 25G needle.
Inject 50 μL of cell suspension into the subcutis in the right hind limb, just under the skin below the kneecap to ensure subcutaneous injection.
Measure body weights on a scale before measuring tumor sizes.
Disinfect the digital caliper.
Check if the caliper is zeroed correctly: 0.00 should be indicated when the jaws are closed.
Fixate a mouse in your left hand with the right hind limb freely accessible.
Measure the length, width, and depth of the right (grafted) hind limb.
When measuring for the first time, also measure the left non-tumor injected hind limb of each mouse.
Calculate the average limb length for all female mice.
Calculate the average limb length for all male mice.
Measure the tumor injected hind limb using the formula: (length × width × depth)/2.
Subtract the volume of the non-tumor injected control limb from the measured tumor limb volume.
Document tumor measurements of each mouse over time.
Begin treatment of mice when tumors reach approximately 50–100 mm².
Anesthetize mice with 2% Isoflurane in 100% oxygen inside a BSC.
Prepare 3 surgical tape sections of approximately 2-3 cm in length per mouse.
Assemble the main part of the transparent mouse restrainer.
Insert the front part into the main part of the mouse restrainer.
Position one mouse into the restrainer with the head at the front.
Slide the roof onto the restrainer.
Slide the bottom into the restrainer, ensuring the mouse’s tail is not stuck and the right hind limb is completely outside.
Pull the right hind limb gently outward and forward.
Place surgical tape behind the limb to secure its position.
Affix the tail to the restrainer roof using surgical tape.
Position the mice in the radiation setup.
Place the restrainer containing one mouse on the bottom lead plate with the right limb facing the center of the setup.
Gently pull the hind limb outward and secure it to the center area with surgical tape on the ankle/paw.
Place the upper protective lead shielding on top of the restrainer.
Repeat these steps for all 4 mice.
Place protective lead on top of the feet (ankle and toes) of the mice.
Place the entire setup inside a transport box.
Take the mouse containing transport box outside of the BSC and bring it to the radiation source.
Place the radiation setup with the mice onto the radiation source.
Adjust the X-ray/radiation beam so that it irradiates a non-shielded center area of 110 mm × 110 mm.
Irradiate with a dose of 2 Gy at 220 kVp, 13 mA applied.
Repeat steps daily to deliver a total fractionated dose of 20 Gy over ten fractions in two weeks.
Document tumor growth of each mouse three times a week during treatment and after until tumors reach maximum size.
Bring bucket with ice, 4% PFA in container, labels, tissue cassette, microcentrifuge tubes, cryovial tubes, scissors, tweezers, scalpels, petri dishes to the animal facility.
Anesthetize mice with 2% isoflurane in 100% oxygen for 5 minutes.
Sacrifice mice according to local legislation and ethical guidelines (e.g., cervical dislocation).
Disinfect the right hind limb area with Virkon thoroughly.
Label tissue cassette.
Screwcap microcentrifuge tube.
Label viable freezing vial.
Harvest tumor from the hind leg of the mice.
Place tumor on a 100 mm² petri dish.
Cut tumor into three sections with scalpel.
Divide each section equally from edge to center.
Place one tissue section inside a labeled tissue cassette.
Place one tissue section into a 0.5 mL screw cap microcentrifuge tube and put on ice.
Place one tissue section into a viable freezing vial and put on ice.
Take samples from mice facility to Biosafety level 1 laboratory.
Snap freeze tissue.
Add liquid nitrogen in a Dewar carrying flask.
Take samples from ice and submerge screw cap vials in liquid nitrogen.
Store labeled vials at −80°C until further analyses.
Get freezing container ("Mr. Frosty") out of −80°C freezer in advance.
Take the cryovial from ice, clean it with 70% EtOH and place into a BSC.
Add 0.5 mL freezing medium to cryovial containing the tissue.
Place the vials in a freezing container and freeze the tissue overnight (16 h).
Place vials following day in the liquid nitrogen freezer.
Submerge the cassette in 4% buffered PFA, in a closed container.
Next day remove the 4% PFA and replace by 70% ethanol for 1–7 days.
Process tissue and stain for hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) according to Aziz et al.
Assess histology of the tissue by H&E staining.
Determine the boundaries of the tumor tissue.
Immunohistochemically stain tissue for γ-H2AX with a subtle Hematoxylin background according to Nagelkerke et al.10.
Validate radiation efficacy by induction of γ-H2AX immunohistochemistry in the tumor tissue established with H&E staining.
